title: R[x] inside the fraction field of a normal Nagata domain is N-1
statement: Let $R$ be a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] which is a Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], let $K$ be its field of fractions, let $x\in K$, and let $S=R[x]\subseteq K$ be the subring of $K$ generated by $R$ and $x$ (an integral domain with field of fractions $K$). Then $S$ is N-1 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]: the integral closure of $S$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated $S$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 0334 (proposition-nagata-universally-japanese, line 46067), proof: statement (***) at the end of Step 4 (line 46126), proved in Step 5 (line 46131 to the end of the proof, line 46221), which uses Lemmas 0333 (lemma-characterize-N-1), 032K (lemma-finite-extension-N-2), 032T (lemma-quasi-finite-over-nagata), 032U (lemma-nagata-localize), 0330 (lemma-criterion-analytically-unramified), 032Y (lemma-analytically-unramified-easy), 0331 (lemma-local-nagata-domain-analytically-unramified), Theorem 00FV (theorem-nullstellensatz) and the lemmas make-integral-trivial and normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1

proof.text: If $x=0$, then $S=R$ is normal [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], hence its integral closure in $K$ is $R$ itself and it is N-1. Assume $x\ne0$ and write $x=b/a$ with $a,b\in R$, $a\ne0$. Since $R$ is Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], its one-generator algebra $S=R[x]$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Inverting $a$ gives $S_a=R_a$, because $x=b/a\in R_a$; this ring is normal by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-n1-local-characterization] reduces the claim to proving $S_{\mathfrak m}$ is N-1 for each maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset S$.

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 0334 (proposition-nagata-universally-japanese), Step 5, lines 46131-46135; Lemma Tag 0333 (lemma-characterize-N-1)

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak m$ and set $\mathfrak n=R\cap\mathfrak m$. The field $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ is generated as a $\kappa(\mathfrak n)$-algebra by the residue of $x$, because $S=R[x]$; it is finite over $\kappa(\mathfrak n)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma]. Let $\bar f(T)=T^d+\sum_{i=1}^d\bar c_iT^{d-i}\in\kappa(\mathfrak n)[T]$ be the monic minimal polynomial of the residue of $x$. Lift each $\bar c_i$ to a fraction $c_i/s_i\in R_{\mathfrak n}$ with $s_i\in R\setminus\mathfrak n$; localize $R$ and $S$ at the product $s=\prod_i s_i$, so all lifts lie in $R_s$. The resulting monic $f(T)\in R_s[T]$ has $f(x)\in\mathfrak mS_s$, since its residue in $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ is $\bar f(\bar x)=0$. The maximal ideal $\mathfrak mS_s$ and its localization of $S$ still give the original $S_{\mathfrak m}$.

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 0334 (proposition-nagata-universally-japanese), Step 5, lines 46137-46144 ('details omitted' for the monic polynomial); the denominator lift is written here

proof.text: Work over the localized $R_s$ and rename it $R$. Adjoin roots of $f$ successively to $K$; at most $d$ finite algebraic extensions give a finite splitting field $K''/K$. Let $R'$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $K''$. The Nagata property of $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-nagata-localization] makes $R'$ a finite $R$-module by the N-2 clause of [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] and [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]; it is a normal domain with fraction field $K''$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal], and Nagata by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-nagata-nagata]. Every root of the monic polynomial $f$ is integral over $R$, so lies in $R'$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Put $S'=R'[x]\subset K''$. The same finitely many $R$-module generators of $R'$ generate $S'$ as an $S$-module, so $S\subseteq S'$ is finite [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], hence integral by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. Every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $S$ has a prime ideal of $S'$ above it by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over], and that prime is maximal by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal].

We claim that every local ring $S'_{\mathfrak m'}$ at a maximal ideal over $\mathfrak m$ is N-1. Since $f(x)\in\mathfrak m'$, the factorization $f(T)=\prod_{i=1}^d(T-r_i)$ with $r_i\in R'$ gives $x-r_i\in\mathfrak m'$ for some $i$. Replace the generator $x$ by $y=x-r_i$; then $S'=R'[y]$ and $y\in\mathfrak m'$. Rename $(R',S',y,\mathfrak m')$ as $(R,S,x,\mathfrak m)$ for this local calculation. Thus the local calculation assumes a normal Nagata domain $R$, $0\ne x\in\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, $S=R[x]$, and a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ containing $x$. If the new $x=0$, then $S=R$ is normal and the local ring is N-1 immediately; otherwise continue.

Let $I=\ker(R[T]\to S)$, where $T\mapsto x$. We show by induction on degree that $I$ is generated by the linear polynomials $cT-d$ with $c,d\in R$ and $cx=d$ in $K$. The degree-zero case is zero because $R\hookrightarrow K$ is injective. If $g(T)=c_dT^d+\cdots+c_0\in I$ with $d>0$, [lem-weil-pbc-leading-coefficient-times-root-integral] says $c_dx$ is integral over $R$; normality [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] gives $d_0:=c_dx\in R$. Then $c_dT-d_0\in I$, and $g-(c_dT-d_0)T^{d-1}$ is in $I$ with degree below $d$. Hence $S/xS\cong R[T]/(I,T)\cong R/J$ with $J=\{d_0\in R: d_0=cx\text{ for some }c\in R\}=R\cap xR$. This identifies the quotient map $R\to S/xS$ and its kernel explicitly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-fractional-principal-quotient-ass] to the nonzero $x$: $R/J$ has no embedded associated primes, and each associated prime $\mathfrak p$ has height one. Under the surjection $S\to S/xS\cong R/J$, the annihilator of a class pulls back from its annihilator in $R/J$; thus the associated primes of $S/xS$ are the inverse images $\mathfrak q$ of those $\mathfrak p$, each minimal over $xS$. Localization at $\mathfrak m$ keeps only $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak m$ and preserves this property, so $S_{\mathfrak m}/xS_{\mathfrak m}$ has no embedded primes. For one such $\mathfrak q$, put $\mathfrak p=R\cap\mathfrak q$. The Noetherian normal local domain $R_{\mathfrak p}$ has dimension one, hence is a discrete valuation ring by [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr]. Since $x\in\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$, $x$ cannot have negative valuation in $R_{\mathfrak p}$: otherwise $x^{-1}\in\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$, contradicting $1=xx^{-1}\in\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$. Therefore $x\in R_{\mathfrak p}$, so $S\otimes_RR_{\mathfrak p}=R_{\mathfrak p}[x]=R_{\mathfrak p}$. The prime $\mathfrak q$ extends to a prime of this local ring containing $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$, hence exactly its maximal ideal $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$; localizing gives $S_{\mathfrak q}=R_{\mathfrak p}$, a regular local ring. These are conditions (2) and (3)(a) of [lem-weil-pbc-analytic-unramified-principal-criterion].

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 0334 (proposition-nagata-universally-japanese), Step 5, lines 46194-46213; Lemma Tag 031T (lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1) and Lemma Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr)

proof.text: For the same associated prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak m$, the quotient $S/\mathfrak q$ is $R/\mathfrak p$: the map $R\to S/\mathfrak q$ is surjective because $x\in\mathfrak q$, and its kernel is $\mathfrak p=R\cap\mathfrak q$. Thus $(S/\mathfrak q)_{\mathfrak m}\cong(R/\mathfrak p)_{\mathfrak n}$, where $\mathfrak n=R\cap\mathfrak m$. The quotient $R/\mathfrak p$ is Nagata by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-nagata-nagata], and its local ring is Nagata by [lem-weil-pbc-nagata-localization]. It is a Noetherian local domain, so its completion is reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-local-nagata-domain-analytically-unramified]. This is condition (3)(b) of [lem-weil-pbc-analytic-unramified-principal-criterion]. That criterion, with $x\ne0$ and $x\in\mathfrak m$, shows $S_{\mathfrak m}$ analytically unramified; [lem-weil-pbc-analytically-unramified-n1] makes it N-1. This completes the local calculation for each $S'_{\mathfrak m'}$ above the original $\mathfrak m$.

proof.text: Return to the finite extension $S\subseteq S'$ of Step 3 and the original maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset S$. The domain $B=(S\setminus\mathfrak m)^{-1}S'$ is finite over $S_{\mathfrak m}$, hence Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] and integral over $S_{\mathfrak m}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. Every maximal ideal of $B$ contracts to the sole maximal ideal of $S_{\mathfrak m}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal]; its contraction to $S'$ is a prime over $\mathfrak m$, hence maximal by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal]. Thus its localization is one of the $S'_{\mathfrak m'}$, N-1 by Steps 4-7. Also $B_a$ is a localization of $S'_a=R'_a$, normal by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain], because the original $x=b/a$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-n1-local-characterization] to $B$: it is N-1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-n1-descends-finite-domain-extension] to the finite extension $S_{\mathfrak m}\subseteq B$: $S_{\mathfrak m}$ is N-1. As the original $\mathfrak m$ was arbitrary, Step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-n1-local-characterization] show $S$ is N-1.
